## Initialize primitives, ghosts and conserved states (`restart_file`) {#sec-ch01-initialization}

### Summary

A block starts from the primitive state the caller hands it: density, velocity, pressure and species fractions
on the interior cells. Initialization checks the shapes, fills the ghost cells, swaps ghosts with the
neighbouring blocks, converts to the conserved state the solver advances, and seeds the passive scalars. A
restart file replaces all of that with saved tensors.

A deck is the YAML input file that configures a run; it is read into the options tree before construction
(@sec-ch01-options; {{< code src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp MeshBlockOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}).
A case is the simulation setup in this report's informal usage: an example driver, its deck and its initial
conditions, such as `examples/straka.cpp` with `examples/straka.yaml` ({{< code examples/straka.cpp >}},
{{< code examples/straka.yaml >}}). **Not provided:** a separate formal case object or case-file schema;
the example accepts a configuration filename and an optional restart filename, not a third case-file input.
A restart file is a saved simulation state from which a run resumes, not a configuration deck. The loader
requires `hydro_u`, `last_time`, `last_cycle`, `file_number` and `next_time`, and restores the saved cycle
and time ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::_init_from_restart >}}); the format and output
schedule are in @sec-ch14-restart.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** N/A, a code map: check shapes, fill and exchange primitive ghosts, convert to conserved rows.

**Data.** In: interior `hydro_w` ($\rho$[^rg-adc30ad62345], $\mathbf v$[^rg-f0f419996146], $p$[^rg-edee3b83dd1a], $y_n$[^rg-d6e8655ff198]) or a restart file. Out: `hydro_u`, `scalar_s`, with ghosts.

**Placement.** Once, after construction and before the first step.

**Activation.** `restart_file` absent: from primitives; present: load the restart (@sec-ch14-restart).

**Guarantee / limits.** A map; no convergence order.

**Evidence.** `test_scalar.<b>` and `test_mesh_multi_block.<b>` (`allclose`, exact shapes); see the Tests layer.
:::

Local symbols: $r_n$[^rg-d926607a7bda] is the mixing ratio of passive scalar $n$ per unit dry mass (`scalar_r`). $r_n^{\mathrm{back}}$
is the ratio recovered by dividing the seeded scalar density by the conserved dry density.

### Derivation

No separate derivation: this section describes an interface or control-flow path, and the operators are derived
in their owning chapters.

### Numerical method

`MeshBlockImpl::initialize` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::initialize >}}) branches to the restart
loader when a file is given and otherwise runs three steps. `initialize_local`
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::initialize_local >}}) checks that `hydro_w` (and `scalar_r` when
scalars exist) has the block's full shape, ghosts included. It saves the outflow background when a radiating face
exists (@sec-ch11-outflow), and fills the physical ghosts of the primitives. The block then exchanges the primitives
and the scalar ratios with its neighbours with interpolation on. `finalize_initialization`
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::finalize_initialization >}}) converts to `hydro_u` with the EOS[^rg-3c222a9e6ef8], seeds
`scalar_s` as the ratio times the conserved dry density. It records the solid fill states with the velocity rows
zeroed when a mask is present (@sec-ch11-solids), and fills the conserved ghosts. Because the exchange precedes the
conversion, the conserved ghosts reflect exchanged primitives. `MeshImpl::initialize`
({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::initialize >}}) runs the fresh path for every local block through the worker
pool and the restart path in a plain loop on the caller's thread. Initialization introduces no accuracy order;
interpolation and boundary accuracy belong to @sec-ch03 and @sec-ch11.

@fig-ch01-initialization-flow shows the call sequence.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch01-initialization-flow
#| fig-cap: "Initialize primitives, ghosts and conserved states. Labelled green boxes name operations or owners; black arrows show the reading sequence, not a timing measurement."
#| fig-alt: "Sequence: shape checks; physical primitive ghosts; primitive exchange; EOS and scalar density; solids / conserved ghosts."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch01.figures.fig_initialization_flow import make_fig
make_fig()
```

**Why the order is exchange, then convert.** Three facts fix it.

1. The ghosts must be filled before the conversion, because the EOS converts every cell, ghosts included. A conserved
   ghost converted from an unfilled primitive ghost would be wrong
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::finalize_initialization >}}).
2. The outflow background is captured before the first physical fill, because the fill overwrites the ghost values the
   background must keep ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::initialize_local >}}).
3. The scalar density is seeded as ratio times the conserved dry density. The ratio the solver later recovers by
   division is then the one the caller gave, up to one rounding per entry. A product and a quotient each round once,
   so $|r_n^{\mathrm{back}} - r_n| \le 2\,\delta_{\mathrm{mach}}\,|r_n|$ with $\delta_{\mathrm{mach}} = 2^{-53}$.

: Implementation anchors for initialization. {#tbl-ch01-initialization-code}

1. Check shapes, save the outflow background, fill physical primitive ghosts: `initialize_local`
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::initialize_local >}}).
2. Exchange the primitives and scalar ratios: `initialize` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::initialize >}}).
3. Convert, seed the scalars, record the solid fills, fill the conserved ghosts: `finalize_initialization`
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::finalize_initialization >}}).
4. For a restart, the writer `write_output_file` ({{< code src/output/restart.cpp RestartOutput::write_output_file >}})
   saved every defined variable except the reconstructible `scalar_r`, plus the clock, cycle and output counters.

**How to use it.** From Python, hand the block the interior primitives with the block's full shape, ghosts
included, and the scalar ratios when the card declares scalars:

```python
vars, t0 = block.initialize({"hydro_w": w, "scalar_r": r})   # fresh start, t0 = 0
```

**The initial-state contract.** S marks a sourced statement; I marks an inference.

#### What snapy does with it

| # | step | detail | source | tag |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 11 | your ghost values at physical faces are overwritten | `initialize_local` fills the physical ghosts with `apply_boundaries`. Only the interior values you give matter there. | [meshblock.cpp#L449](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L449) | S |
| 12 | ghosts between blocks come from the neighbours | Under a mesh the primitives are exchanged (with interpolation) after the local fill. | [meshblock.cpp#L452-L459](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L452-L459) | S |
| 13 | radiating (outflow) faces keep a copy | With a radiating boundary, your `hydro_w` (ghosts included) is cloned as the outflow background **before** the fill. There your ghost values do matter. | [meshblock.cpp#L444-L448](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L444-L448) | S |
| 14 | then the conversion | `hydro_u` = EOS `W->U` of the filled `hydro_w`. | [meshblock.cpp#L486](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L486) | S |
| 15 | hydrostatic balance | **Not required, but you should provide it.** The well-balanced scheme rebuilds a discrete reference from the state on every call. A column marched from the continuum hydrostatic equation is balanced only to $O(\Delta z^2)$, and the remainder is a standing force on an atmosphere meant to be at rest. `balance_column` removes it (@tbl-ch01-initialization-contract-3). | [balance_column.hpp#L15-L19](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/hydro/balance_column.hpp#L15-L19) | S |

#### `balance_column` in one table

This summarizes the initial-state projection; @sec-ch05-balcol gives the full treatment.

Call from C++ `snap::balance_column`, or from Python `snapy.balance_column(w, dx1f, grav, wall_clamp=True, rtol=1e-10, max_iter=120, geometry="", stretched=False)`, bound as `balance_column` ([pyhydro.cpp#L50-L68](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/python/csrc/pyhydro.cpp#L50-L68), S).

| # | item | detail | source | tag |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 16 | `w` | (nvar, nc3, nc2, nx1) primitives of the **whole column with no ghosts**. It is not modified, and rows other than `IDN`, `IPR` pass through. | [balance_column.hpp#L31-L35](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/hydro/balance_column.hpp#L31-L35) | S |
| 17 | `dx1f` | (nx1,) cell widths, same dtype and device as `w`; refused otherwise. | [balance_column.cpp#L21-L25](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/hydro/balance_column.cpp#L21-L25) | S |
| 18 | `grav` | A **positive** downward magnitude, e.g. 9.8, not `grav1`[^rg-76103610383a]; refused if not > 0. | [balance_column.cpp#L18](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/hydro/balance_column.cpp#L18) | S |
| 19 | `wall_clamp` | Must be true and must match `dynamics/wb-wall-clamp` in the card that runs the result. | [balance_column.cpp#L30-L33](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/hydro/balance_column.cpp#L30-L33); [balance_column.hpp#L43-L48](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/hydro/balance_column.hpp#L43-L48) | S |
| 20 | other refusals | Fewer than 5 cells; $p\le0$ or $\rho\le0$ anywhere; under `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT`, any geometry other than `"cartesian"`. | [balance_column.cpp#L35-L40](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/hydro/balance_column.cpp#L35-L40), [#L47-L48](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/hydro/balance_column.cpp#L47-L48), [#L53-L54](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/hydro/balance_column.cpp#L53-L54) | S |
| 21 | what it does | Iterates $p_i \leftarrow p_{\mathrm{ref},i}(p) + C$, $\rho_i \leftarrow p_i/(p_i/\rho_i)_0$. **It holds $p/\rho$ fixed per cell**, so it holds the temperature fixed for `ideal-gas`, and for `ideal-moist` at fixed mass fractions. | [balance_column.hpp#L20-L29](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/hydro/balance_column.hpp#L20-L29) | S |
| 22 | what it returns | (balanced w, residual, sweeps). The residual is $\max\lvert p'-C\rvert/(\rho g\Delta z)$, the leftover acceleration in units of $g$; `sweeps` is 0 for a column already balanced. | [balance_column.hpp#L52-L60](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/hydro/balance_column.hpp#L52-L60) | S |
| 23 | failure | It throws if `rtol` is not reached in `max_iter` sweeps, or if the column diverges. | [balance_column.cpp#L94-L102](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/hydro/balance_column.cpp#L94-L102) | S |
| 24 | **limit: the column moves** | $C$ is a free constant read at the top cell. The surface pressure, column mass and any anchor level you chose do **not** survive. The source quotes 2.5e-4 of $p$ on a Neptune-like column and 1.2e-2 on a 300 km giant-planet one. Re-pin what you need against the balanced column, inside your own loop. | [balance_column.hpp#L83-L89](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/hydro/balance_column.hpp#L83-L89) | S |
| 25 | limit: what you must guarantee | Physical (not periodic) $x_1$ boundaries; at least 5 $x_1$ cells in every block the column is later split into; the same uniform-or-stretched classification as every block; and, if moist, re-saturate and iterate. | [balance_column.hpp#L66-L81](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/hydro/balance_column.hpp#L66-L81) | S |

: Initialization contract, table 3. {#tbl-ch01-initialization-contract-3}

#### Minimal correct examples at the pin

1. **Dry, C++ (the preface's Straka deck).** `initialize_block` builds a float64 `(nvar, nc3, nc2, nc1)` tensor on the device ([straka.cpp#L82-L84](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/examples/straka.cpp#L82-L84)). It takes $g$ = `-grav1` (#L62) and $R_d$ = `Rgas/weight` (#L69). It sets an adiabatic $T(x_1)$, then $p$, then adds the cold bubble to $T$[^rg-1c45304f6b95] and sets $\rho = p/(R_dT)$. Velocity stays 0. It hands over `vars["hydro_w"]` (#L86-L93) and, with scalars, a `scalar_r` with the same spatial shape (#L95-L102): [straka.cpp#L53-L104](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/examples/straka.cpp#L53-L104) [S]. It fills every cell from the cell centres, ghosts included; the fill then overwrites the physical ghosts (row 11) [S]. It does not call `balance_column`.
2. **Python, smallest.** Excerpt (lines 26 and 31–35; lines 27–30 move the block to a device and read the EOS floor) of [test: L26–35](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/tests/test_check_redo_floor.py#L26-L35) [S]:

   ```python
   block = MeshBlock(MeshBlockOptions.from_yaml(yaml_file))
   # Shape: (nvar, nc3, nc2, nc1)
   w = dict(block.named_buffers())["hydro.D"].clone().zero_()
   w[kIDN] = 1.0
   w[kIPR] = 1.0e5
   w[kICY] = 1.0e-3
   block_vars, _ = block.initialize({"hydro_w": w})
   ```
   This test state is uniform and has no gravity balance. It is a shape-and-call example, not an atmosphere at rest [I, from the four lines].
3. **With `balance_column` (moist, C++).** `examples/bryan.cpp` `project` passes the interior x1 column, its `dx1f`, `wall_clamp=true` and the grid's `stretched_x1()` ([bryan.cpp#L204-L217](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/examples/bryan.cpp#L204-L217)). `balance_ic` requires the whole x1 column in one block and the clamp on (#L222-L228). It is switched on by `problem/balance-ic: true` (#L372-L375) [S].
4. **A column built by marching, and which spacing it steps by (C++).** The three moist example drivers do not
   fill the column from a closed form: they put the surface state half a cell above the bottom face and then step
   an adiabat from one cell centre to the next, writing each centre as they pass it
   ({{< code examples/run_hydro.cpp main >}}, {{< code examples/bryan.cpp initialize_block >}},
   {{< code examples/jupiter_evap_precip_1d.cpp initialize_block >}}). The step from centre $i$[^rg-3f39479eeb50] to centre $i+1$
   must be the **centre spacing** `dx1v[i + 1]`, not the cell width `dx1f[i]`; the isothermal continuation above
   the adiabat steps centre $i-1$ to centre $i$ and so takes `dx1v[i]`. The first half-step, from the bottom face
   to the first centre, is `dx1f[il] / 2`, which is the midpoint offset of that cell.

   On a grid whose $x_1$ cells are all the same width the two spacings are equal and the distinction does not
   arise; on a stretched one they differ by half the change in width across the face, and using the cell width
   accumulates that difference all the way up the column. `tests/test_example_ic_stretched.py` (ctest
   `test_example_ic_stretched_python`) runs `run_hydro` for zero steps on a dry 300 km, 64-cell column with
   $g=22$ $\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$, uniform and then with `cells/x1rat` $1/1.058$ and $1.058$, and compares the
   initial pressure at every centre with the analytic dry adiabat: the stretched error must stay within six times
   the uniform error of the same driver ({{< code tests/test_example_ic_stretched.py >}}). Its header records
   that stepping by the cell width instead left the pressure at the top of that column off by about 35 %. The
   ctest was not run for this report: **pending a pinned ctest run**.

   Write your own builder the same way: march the centres with `dx1v`, and reserve `dx1f` for what the cell
   contains rather than for how far the next centre is.

In Python a restart goes through `block.initialize_from_restart(path)`; in C++ the path is the second argument of
`initialize`. Both return the saved time instead of zero.

Refused: a `hydro_w` or `scalar_r` whose shape is not (variables, $x_3$, $x_2$, $x_1$) of the block, and a missing
`scalar_r` when the card declares scalars. The `hydro_w` refusal names the expected shape in its message; the two
`scalar_r` refusals say only that the tensor is required or has an incorrect shape
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::initialize_local >}}). The lines that
capture the outflow background and fill the physical ghosts are these
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::initialize_local >}}):

```cpp
// Capture before any physical face fill, independently of mutable inputs.
if (has_radiating_boundary()) {
  vars["boundary_reference_w"] = hydro_w.clone();
  if (scalar_r.defined()) vars["boundary_reference_r"] = scalar_r.clone();
}
apply_boundaries(vars, hydro_w, scalar_r, true);
```

The assertions are in {{< code tests/test_scalar.cpp DeviceTest.initialize_and_transport_scalar >}} and, through
`side_is_uniform` ({{< code tests/test_mesh_multi_block.cpp side_is_uniform >}}), in

at the pin: **pending a pinned ctest run**. No report check exists for this section.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
The restart branch returns before the primitive exchange and relies on the saved tensors' ghosts. No
fresh-versus-restart ghost equivalence is measured here.
:::

<!-- reader glossary notes -->
[^rg-adc30ad62345]: $\rho$ — total density, dry plus every species that carries mass [kg m$^{-3}$]

[^rg-f0f419996146]: $\mathbf v = (v_1,v_2,v_3)$ — velocity [m s$^{-1}$]

[^rg-edee3b83dd1a]: $p$ — pressure [Pa]

[^rg-d6e8655ff198]: $y_n$ — mass fraction of species $n$ **per unit total mass**, $\rho_n = \rho y_n$, dimensionless [-]; this is snapy's composition variable and the only one the state vector carries

[^rg-d926607a7bda]: $r_n$ — mass mixing ratio of species $n$ **per unit dry mass**, $r_n = \rho_n/\rho_{\mathrm{d}}$, dimensionless [-]; used only where the code is per dry air (passive tracers, @sec-ch10-tracer). Never written $r$ without its species subscript, because $r$ alone is the radius (§1)

[^rg-3c222a9e6ef8]: EOS — equation of state

[^rg-76103610383a]: grav1 — gravity component along the first coordinate

[^rg-1c45304f6b95]: $T$ — temperature [K]

[^rg-3f39479eeb50]: $i, j, k$ — cell indices in $x_1, x_2, x_3$
<!-- end reader glossary notes -->
